a_theLadder.description: src/DungeonFortress.Presentation/RoomGeometry.cs — the three bases and the predicate that picks between them. This is the change itself: what a room's border is inset by, and on what evidence.

mutants.name: a-i: the side-wall base buys nothing
mutants.edit: public const double SideWallClearance = (WallRenderGeometry.EdgeReferenceWidth / 2.0) + BorderStrokeHalfWidth + WallVisibleGap; -> = PlainBorderBase;
mutants.result: FAILED: 4 of 451. The_border_of_every_room_clears_every_wall_band_on_every_side at all three tile sizes — quarters@19,2 goes straight back to 0.375 reference px on West and East, which is the defect the issue was opened on — plus Overlapping_rooms_with_different_wall_profiles_collide_no_more_than_before, because with the side base collapsed onto the plain one the collision moves back to the plain-against-north pair the debt ledger named.

mutants.name: a-ii: the north base loses the half-seam #139 missed
mutants.edit: NorthWallClearance drops the (WallRenderGeometry.EdgeReferenceWidth / 2.0) term, i.e. reverts to Issue #139's 5.0
mutants.result: FAILED: 7 of 451. The_border_of_every_room_clears_every_wall_band_on_every_side at all three sizes (farm@1,1 North falls to 0.375 reference px — #139's residual, reproduced), A_wall_in_front_of_a_room_cannot_be_cleared_by_any_inset at all three (its un-excused sweep now reports a North row, which a wall in front cannot produce), and Overlapping_rooms_with_different_wall_profiles_collide_no_more_than_before (5.0 - 2.0 = 3.0 is a step of the purpose ladder, so the pairs collide differently).

mutants.name: a-iii: WallSides stops reading the column beside the cell
mutants.edit: for (var row = cell.Y - 1; row <= cell.Y + 1; row++) -> for (var row = cell.Y; row <= cell.Y; row++), i.e. straight neighbours only, no diagonals
mutants.result: FAILED: 1 of 451 — WallSides_reads_straight_neighbours_north_and_south_and_columns_beside. Deliberately recorded as a one-test kill: the shipped map does NOT catch this, because quarters@19,2 has orthogonal west and east neighbours as well as the north-west diagonal at (18,1), so its inset is unchanged and the whole-map sweep stays green. The unit test is the only thing standing between this branch and a first player-painted room whose only wall is a diagonal.

b_theWallAsDrawn.description: src/DungeonFortress.Presentation/WorldRenderGeometry.cs — the other half of the arithmetic. Every clearance above is measured against what the wall actually paints, and the difference between the wall's lines and the wall's pixels is the whole mechanism of this issue.

mutants.name: b-i: DrawnBands stops widening a seam into the band it is painted as
mutants.edit: var half = ReferenceStrokeWidth(stroke.Kind) * scale / 2.0; -> var half = 0.0 * ReferenceStrokeWidth(stroke.Kind) * scale / 2.0;
mutants.result: FAILED: 4 of 451 — A_walls_side_seam_paints_half_its_width_into_the_next_cell, and The_pre_147_ladder_really_did_draw_the_border_inside_the_wall at all three tile sizes. The second group is the important one: with seams treated as zero-width lines the pre-#147 ladder stops violating anything, which is exactly the blind spot that let Issue #139 measure a 6.14 px gap where the drawn gap was 0.68.

c_adapterWiring.description: src/DungeonFortress.Game/Main.cs — the four points that connect the pure change to the drawn frame. None is reachable from a pure test (ADR 0011 keeps the engine assembly out of Presentation.Tests), so all four are proven through AdapterSource reading Main.cs as text, the technique HudReadabilityTests and Issue #139 already use.

d_theCeilingAndTheUnits.description: The supporting decision the change forced: what the ladder is bounded against, now that the deepest rung is 8.625 and no longer fits the '32 / 4.0' the tests carried. Both constants are reference-pixel, and the mistake they replace was comparing reference pixels against screen ones.

mutants.name: d-i: the ceiling goes back to a quarter of a cell
mutants.edit: public const double MaximumBorderInset = (ReferenceCell / 2.0) - BorderStrokeHalfWidth; -> = ReferenceCell / 4.0;
mutants.result: FAILED: 1 of 451 — Wall_aware_insets_are_still_distinct_and_bounded. At 5.5 the bound rejects every wall-aware rung, which is the honest answer to why '32 / 4.0' could not simply have its units corrected in place: at the correct units it was already false before this issue, at 8.0.

mutants.name: d-ii: ReferenceCell stops being CameraView's
mutants.result: FAILED: 4 of 451 — ReferenceCell_is_the_one_CameraView_scales_by (the executable pin through CameraView.WorldVisualScale(44), which replaces the comment that used to say 'restated from CameraView.cs:108'), and A_wall_in_front_of_a_room_cannot_be_cleared_by_any_inset at all three tile sizes, because a wider cell raises MaximumBorderInset above the 10.0 a wall in front would cost and the declared exception stops being justified.

notCovered: No mutant targets RoomGeometry.BorderEdges' cell/side attribution on its own: every existing outline test (A_single_cell_is_a_closed_inset_square, A_room_is_one_outline_and_not_a_box_per_cell, An_inner_corner_closes_instead_of_leaving_a_gap, A_room_with_a_hole_draws_the_hole_as_well, No_segment_leaves_the_bounding_box_of_the_room, The_default_rooms_of_the_shipped_map_all_close) runs through it, because Border now delegates to it. Breaking it breaks them.

The excuse for a wall standing in front of a room is asserted, not mutated: A_wall_in_front_of_a_room_cannot_be_cleared_by_any_inset checks the arithmetic that makes it necessary and the WorldDrawOrder declaration that stands in for it, and d-ii above shows the arithmetic half is live.
